objectives: Recognize confusion, hypotension, and tachypnea as danger signs requiring immediate referral-level care.
Start pre-referral stabilization and treatment without delaying for full outpatient workup.
Document and communicate referral details clearly to protect continuity of care.
takeaways: Confusion plus BP 86/54 and RR 32/min is not uncomplicated malaria at HC III.
Give pre-referral emergency care first; do not wait for full diagnostics before transfer.
A complete referral note should include danger signs, interventions, and transfer time.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A confused febrile adult arrives hypotensive and tachypneic. Decide what to do now, what not to delay, and how to hand over safely.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: High fever, confusion, and weakness since yesterday

sections.title: Family report
sections.text: Wife says he became confused this morning and has barely taken fluids.

coach.title: Daniel is critically unwell
coach.body: He is drowsy, answers slowly, and cannot sit unsupported for long. Start by deciding whether this is safe for outpatient management.
coach.quote: “He is not himself and keeps drifting off.”

teach.label: Clinical framing
teach.text: In febrile adults, altered mental status and shock physiology move you immediately toward emergency stabilization and referral.

critical.title: Danger signs present
critical.body: Confusion + hypotension + tachypnea indicate severe febrile illness.

coach.title: What is the safest first move?
coach.body: Choose the action that matches Daniel's current physiology, not a routine fever flow.

options.text: Begin emergency stabilization, classify as severe febrile illness, and prepare urgent referral immediately
Start oral artemether-lumefantrine and observe in OPD for 6 hours
Give paracetamol first and wait to see if confusion settles before deciding
Wait for malaria RDT before deciding whether referral is needed

question.right: Correct. With confusion, BP 86/54, and RR 32/min, this patient meets danger-sign referral threshold now. Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 support immediate stabilization and urgent transfer rather than outpatient observation.
question.wrong: Re-check this chart: confusion, hypotension (86/54), and tachypnea (32/min) make outpatient care unsafe. Delaying referral for oral AL, antipyretics, or test confirmation risks deterioration.

coach.title: Treat before transfer
coach.body: Transport is being arranged. Choose the intervention bundle that addresses his immediate risks.

question.prompt: Which immediate action bundle is best before transfer?

options.text: Correct hypoglycemia, give pre-referral severe-malaria treatment per protocol, start fluids, and transfer urgently
Wait for malaria RDT result before giving any antimalarial treatment
Give only oral AL because malaria is likely, then send once he can swallow
Give broad-spectrum oral antibiotics and ask family to return tomorrow if worse

question.right: Correct. Glucose 2.6 mmol/L and altered mental status require immediate correction and pre-referral emergency treatment now. Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 emphasize not delaying life-saving care while referral is underway.
question.wrong: This patient is unstable now: low glucose, confusion, and hypotension cannot wait for routine sequencing. Pre-referral emergency treatment and urgent transfer are safer than oral-only or delayed plans.

codes.code: Suspected severe malaria / severe febrile illness
codes.name: Referral emergency

coach.title: What must be communicated?
coach.body: A weak referral note can undo good emergency care. Choose the strongest handover.

question.prompt: What should your referral communication include?

options.text: Document vitals, danger signs, treatments already given, and call receiving unit with ETA
Write only 'fever' and leave receiving team to reassess from the start
Delay transfer until every test result is finalized
Send patient without paperwork because caregiver can explain

question.right: Correct. Clear handover with Daniel's abnormal vitals and interventions supports continuity and faster receiving-facility decisions.
question.wrong: This case has high-risk instability. Minimal or delayed handover increases transfer risk and repeats work at the receiving center.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: Recognized severe febrile danger signs and initiated urgent pre-referral care.
sections.emphasis: Outpatient oral malaria treatment alone was unsafe for this presentation.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: Daniel's confusion, BP 86/54, RR 32/min, and poor oral intake required emergency referral logic from the first minute. Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 support immediate stabilization and pre-referral treatment without waiting for complete outpatient diagnostics.

teach.label: Clinician review
teach.text: In severe febrile illness, triage physiology drives decisions: stabilize, treat immediate threats, and transfer with strong documentation.
